rationale: C14 provides the closest concrete drafting template. Both proclamations recite a park-establishing statute, identify a separate statutory provision authorizing presidential action after specified prerequisites, affirm that those statutory conditions have been fully complied with, and then use that authority to place extensively described lands into a national park. This distinctive predicate-to-compliance-to-land-dedication sequence is more probative than their shared subject matter or routine proclamation boilerplate. C15 and C11 are weaker establishment precedents involving donated historic lands and metes-and-bounds descriptions, but they lack C14's closely parallel statutory-compliance machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas section 1 of an act approved July 25, 1956 ... provides that when ... non-Federal lands ... shall have been acquired and transferred ... to the United States ... such area shall be dedicated and set apart as the Horseshoe Bend National Military Park
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas section 1 of the act of June 29, 1938 ... established the Olympic National Park ... Whereas section 5 of the said act provides in part as follows
shared_material.explanation: Both open the operative legal case by identifying the park statute and then detailing the statutory conditions governing presidential addition or dedication of lands.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas the requirements of sections 1 and 2 of the act of July 25, 1956 ... have been fully complied with
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas it appears that the terms and conditions of the said act of June 29, 1938, have been fully complied with as to such lands
shared_material.explanation: This is a notably close compliance recital linking completion of statutory prerequisites directly to the proclamation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 4 of the above-mentioned act ... do hereby dedicate and set aside the following-described lands ... as the Horseshoe Bend National Military Park
shared_material.parent_excerpt: under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by the above-quoted provisions of section 5 ... the following-described lands ... are hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Olympic national Park
shared_material.explanation: The operative clauses use closely parallel authority citations and immediately apply them to lengthy legal descriptions of lands placed within a national park.
